headline: Why an exponentially long state can still have a short preparation rule
thesis: The state has one amplitude for every grid point, but those amplitudes are not independent data. They all come from the same three-piece Hermite profile. The construction keeps that functional structure while reading the binary address, so the circuit carries only a small working state whose dimension depends on the smoothing order k.

baselineObjects.body: This is what we mean by a sample table: write down all N function values as if they were unrelated input data. It is correct, but it immediately forgets that every entry came from one simple function.

This is the reference preparation tree: each prefix stores the probability mass under that prefix, and its two child masses determine the next controlled rotation. The tree is transparent, but the number of prefixes grows with the number of samples.

question: Can we prepare exactly the same amplitudes without first materializing the full amplitude list or its full binary mass tree?

compressionSteps.title: Do not turn the Hermite profile into unrelated samples
compressionSteps.body: The left tail, polynomial bridge and right tail each have a finite description. The proof keeps those descriptions alive instead of expanding them into N separate numbers.

compressionSteps.title: A binary digit only chooses the next dyadic half-interval
compressionSteps.body: Reading the address most-significant-bit first is an interval walk. We only need to update enough information to evaluate the same source function on the chosen child interval.

compressionSteps.title: Tails need scalars; the polynomial needs Bernstein coefficients
compressionSteps.formula: e^{\pm p_j}:\text{ scalar update},\qquad c\mapsto M_{b_s}c,\quad c\in\mathbb R^{2k+2}
compressionSteps.body: The exponential pieces factor over address bits. On the polynomial piece, exact de Casteljau subdivision maps one short Bernstein coefficient vector to the left or right child vector. Boundary bookkeeping plus the two tails gives total width D=2k+6.

compressionSteps.title: The bit-by-bit finite-state rule is exactly an MPS/TT factorization
compressionSteps.body: The long amplitude vector is represented by n_p local tensors coupled through a D-dimensional bond. The bond is working memory, not another copy of the amplitude table.

compressionSteps.title: Canonicalize locally, complete isometries, then emit elementary gates
compressionSteps.body: Small Gram contractions give the norm; thin LQ makes the chain locally norm preserving; only reachable columns are completed to real unitaries and decomposed into rotations. The bond qubits return to zero.

crossPollination.idea: Supplies the smooth three-piece profile and the low-degree polynomial bridge.
Bernstein coordinates and exact de Casteljau subdivision turn a polynomial into a stable left/right interval update rule.
The finite update state is reinterpreted as the bond of a matrix-product state / tensor train.
Local isometries are completed and decomposed into an explicit clean Ry/CNOT circuit.

evolution.title: Candidate and proof progression — how the certified construction changed
evolution.provenance: No generation counter or model-active runtime was persisted for this historical search. To avoid inventing one, the page reports auditable Git certification milestones. The 22 h 56 min 06 s below is repository wall-clock between the first baseline certificate and the first polynomial-gate certificate, not continuous agent compute time.
evolution.comparisonBoundary: These two resource displays have different scopes: the reference tuple is the saved k=1, n_p=3 example, while the new entry is an all-width symbolic family bound. Therefore ASPBE does not label this pair a strict same-instance lexicographic winner. The certified advance is structural and asymptotic: for fixed k, the new quantum bound is linear in n_p rather than expanding an arbitrary 2^{n_p}-entry table.

stages.label: Certified baseline
stages.scope: Displayed resource tuple is the preserved k=1, n_p=3, L=1 finite example.
stages.reading: Compute all sample masses, recursively split them by binary prefixes, and compile the resulting uniformly controlled rotations. This route is exact and pedagogically transparent, but it does not exploit the special function family when forming the preparation data.

stages.label: Structural family certificate
stages.scope: All-width exact-real quantum family for arbitrary natural k, n_p>=1 and positive L.
stages.reading: Keep the function in Bernstein / finite-state form, reinterpret that update rule as a bounded-bond tensor train, canonicalize the local maps and compile them to Ry/CNOT while cleaning the bond register.

topology.title: What changed in the proof graph
topology.summary: The topological contribution is a change of factorization. The old route first forgets the generating function and expands it into explicit samples. The new route inserts a bridge from Bernstein subdivision to tensor-network memory, so the proof reaches the circuit compiler without passing through an exponentially large amplitude-list object.

contributions.title: Approximation theory ↔ tensor networks
contributions.body: Bernstein subdivision turns a continuous polynomial representation into the local transition matrices of a tensor train.

contributions.title: Source function → circuit without materializing the full amplitude list
contributions.body: The proof no longer factors through one independent stored number for every grid point.

contributions.title: Tensor-train compilation becomes reusable
contributions.body: Norm contraction, canonicalization, local isometry completion and primitive compilation can support future structured state-preparation families.

contributions.title: Complexity is indexed by internal width
contributions.body: For this family the useful structural parameter is D=2k+6, while 2^{n_p} is the ambient vector length.
